articles.title: Inspiring age-gap love story: “She’s been through the whole process and she’s been very helpful to me”- how Jordon Hudson became an important part of Bill Belichick’s life
articles.summary: NFL News: Bill Belichick has spent most of his life talking about football, not his personal life. So when the legendary coach opened up about Jordon Hudson dur.
articles.body: Bill Belichick has spent most of his life talking about football, not his personal life. So when the legendary coach opened up about Jordon Hudson during a 2025 interview with Michael Strahan on Good Morning America, even a simple comment stood out. Belichick described Hudson as “terrific through the whole process” and said she had been “very helpful” to him. He explained that she handled business matters unrelated to North Carolina football, giving him more time to focus on coaching. While their relationship has received plenty of attention because of their age difference and Belichick’s public profile, his own words offered a different picture: one centered on support, trust, companionship and helping each other through a major stage of life.What did Bill Belichick mean when he said Jordon Hudson was “very helpful” to him?Belichick’s explanation was actually quite straightforward. He said Hudson helped him with “the business things that don’t relate to North Carolina” that came up in his life. That allowed him to concentrate on football, which remained his main priority.For Belichick, that was no small thing. After spending decades in the NFL, including a historic run with the New England Patriots, he was entering an entirely different chapter when he became head coach at the University of North Carolina.The move meant learning a new environment while dealing with the demands that come with being one of the most recognizable coaches in American football. At the same time, Belichick had other commitments, including media appearances and work connected to his book, The Art of Winning.His comments suggest that Hudson helped take care of some responsibilities away from the football field. In other words, she helped create room for him to concentrate on the job he cared about most.That makes the quote more meaningful than it may first appear. Belichick was not simply calling Hudson supportive. He was giving a clear example of how her presence helped him manage his life.How did Jordon Hudson support Belichick during his new chapter?The timing of Belichick’s comments is important. His relationship with Hudson became public during a period when almost everything around his personal life was attracting attention.At the same time, he was trying to begin a new professional chapter at North Carolina. After years of working in the NFL, the college game brought new responsibilities, new expectations and a completely different setting.Belichick said Hudson helped him with matters outside North Carolina football so that he could keep his attention on coaching. That description gives a picture of a relationship where support was not necessarily about grand gestures. Sometimes, it was about handling the things that could distract him from his work.He also spoke about Hudson’s contribution to The Art of Winning. Belichick said she helped with the tribute pages and brought a business perspective to the project. He admitted that he could sometimes become too technical when discussing football and said Hudson did a good job of keeping him “on balance.”That detail is particularly revealing because it shows that Belichick valued her opinion even in an area closely connected to his own expertise.She was not simply standing beside him while he worked. According to Belichick, she offered another perspective.What does their age-gap relationship say about love and companionship?Belichick and Hudson have faced constant attention because of their significant age difference. Their relationship has been discussed far beyond the football world, with many people focusing on the years between them rather than the way they describe their connection.But Belichick’s own comments offer another way to look at their relationship.When asked about Hudson, he did not try to turn the conversation into a dramatic romantic story. Instead, he talked about the things that mattered to him: support, trust, another perspective and having someone who could help him handle parts of his life outside football.That can be an important part of any relationship, regardless of age.People at different stages of life can still find common ground through shared interests, respect and companionship. Belichick and Hudson reportedly first met in 2021 on a flight from Boston to Florida, where they had a conversation after Belichick noticed Hudson reading a philosophy book about deductive logic.Their connection later became more visible in public, particularly in 2024.While outsiders may focus heavily on their age difference, Belichick’s own words place the emphasis somewhere else. He described Hudson as someone who had been helpful during an important period of his life.That does not tell the public everything about their relationship, and Belichick has been careful not to share those private details. But it does show that he sees value in having someone beside him who can offer support when his life becomes demanding.Why did Belichick’s simple words feel so meaningful?Perhaps the biggest reason the quote received attention is the person who said it.Belichick is known for being extremely private and often gives short, carefully measured answers when questions move away from football. He rarely turns interviews into detailed discussions about his emotions or relationships.That made his praise of Hudson stand out.Calling her “terrific” and saying she had been “very helpful” may sound simple, but coming from someone as reserved as Belichick, the words offered a rare glimpse into his appreciation for her.He also told Strahan that they had a “good personal relationship” and confirmed that he was happy, while making it clear that he did not want to discuss the private details of their life.That balance says a lot.Belichick was willing to acknowledge Hudson’s importance without opening the door completely to the public. He gave people enough to understand that she mattered to him, while still protecting the relationship from becoming an entirely public story.There was also a touching idea behind his explanation. Belichick has spent much of his life being the person others rely on. As a coach, he was expected to prepare teams, make difficult decisions and lead players through pressure.In this part of his life, however, he was acknowledging that he also benefited from having someone who supported him.His words suggest that Hudson helped him carry some of the responsibilities outside football so that he could continue doing what he loved.And perhaps that is what makes their story more interesting than the headlines about their age difference. At its heart, Belichick’s description was not about numbers. It was about finding someone who could bring support and another point of view during a major change in his life.For a man who has spent decades telling the world about football while saying very little about himself, simply saying that someone has been “very helpful” can say quite a lot.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: NFL legend Adam Vinatieri heads 11,332 feet into the Alps for a Guinness World Record that sounds impossible
articles.summary: NFL News: Adam Vinatieri has already made some of the most iconic kicks in NFL history, but the New England Patriots legend is preparing for perhaps his most un.
articles.body: Adam Vinatieri has already made some of the most iconic kicks in NFL history, but the New England Patriots legend is preparing for perhaps his most unusual challenge yet. The Pro Football Hall of Famer will travel to the Swiss Alps next week to attempt an official Guinness World Records field goal at Jungfraujoch, known as the “Top of Europe,” at an elevation of 3,454 meters (11,332 feet). The Patriots are partnering with Jungfrau Railways for the event as part of the franchise's promotion ahead of its upcoming international game in Munich.Adam Vinatieri set for bizarre Guinness World Record attempt atop the Swiss AlpsIf successful, Vinatieri's kick would establish the highest-elevation field goal ever recorded, according to the Patriots. And the location could not be more fitting for a kicker whose career includes one of the NFL's most famous snow kicks.During the Patriots' 2001 playoff run, he delivered one of the most memorable kicks in franchise history against the Oakland Raiders. With heavy snow falling during the divisional playoff game in January 2002, Vinatieri connected on a 45-yard field goal late in regulation to tie the game.He later kicked the game-winning field goal in overtime, helping New England advance toward its first Super Bowl championship. More than two decades later, the 53-year-old former kicker is preparing to kick in snow again, except this time, he will be doing it thousands of feet above sea level.The conditions will be unlike anything in the NFLThe Patriots will set up goalposts in the snow at Jungfraujoch before Vinatieri attempts the kick.The extreme altitude is expected to make the challenge particularly unusual. The thinner air, snow-covered surface, and mountain weather will create conditions that are very different from a conventional NFL field. Vinatieri acknowledged as much while discussing the upcoming attempt.“I've had the chance to attempt a lot of special kicks in my career, but getting to go for an official Guinness World Records title on snow at 3,454 meters in a Patriots jersey is truly something special,” Vinatieri said.He added that the conditions in the Alps are “completely different” from what players experience in the NFL, which is precisely what makes the challenge exciting.Vinatieri's latest challenge comes after Hall of Fame honorThe record attempt comes during a particularly significant year for Vinatieri.The former Patriots and Indianapolis Colts kicker was recently inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame, adding another major honor to a career that already includes four Super Bowl championships.Vinatieri spent 24 NFL seasons with New England and Indianapolis from 1996 through 2019. He remains the NFL's all-time leading scorer with 2,673 points, according to Guinness World Records. He also holds the NFL record for most career field-goal attempts, with 715, according to the league's record book.Now, he has the opportunity to add another unusual record to his résumé.Why are the Patriots sending Vinatieri to Switzerland?The Guinness World Records attempt isn't happening in isolation. The Patriots are using the event to begin their countdown to their 2026 international game in Munich, where New England will face the Detroit Lions on November 15.The Jungfraujoch event is part of the Patriots' efforts to promote the Munich matchup and connect with fans in the DACH region, Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. That makes Vinatieri a natural choice for the promotional event.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: "Because he’s famous....": Travis Kelce faces brutal verdict over potential NFL broadcasting career as retirement rumors grow
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce may have a future beyond the Kansas City Chiefs, but stepping into an NFL broadcast booth could bring a challenge unlike anything he has .
articles.body: Travis Kelce may have a future beyond the Kansas City Chiefs, but stepping into an NFL broadcast booth could bring a challenge unlike anything he has faced on the field. As retirement talk follows the 36-year-old tight end ahead of his October birthday, his potential move into sports media has sparked a debate. Some analysts question whether his star power would translate into strong game commentary, despite his football experience and growing media presence.Travis Kelce's NFL broadcasting future questioned by media criticsThe discussion took a sharp turn on the September 16 episode of the Awful Announcing podcast. Brendon Kleen pushed back against the growing buzz around Kelce's potential broadcasting career, arguing that his celebrity status may be driving the speculation.“Can I just butt in there?” Brendon Kleen shared on the September 16 episode of the Awful Announcing podcast. “I was going to bring that up after you were done, but there is no evidence Travis Kelce would be interested in or good at calling NFL games. That is made up. It is because he’s famous. That’s it.”Drew Lerner echoed those doubts, cautioning against treating a possible media career as a certainty.“I don’t know if it’s made up. I think there is smoke there because reputable people have talked about this. I know I’m saying Kelce wouldn’t even be good at it,” Drew Lerner added. “ … I just think we are way over our skis just with this assumption that by next year Travis Kelce is going to be like breaking down fourth downs for the Commanders in week nine on a game call.”The criticism comes despite Kelce's 14 seasons of NFL experience and three Super Bowl wins. His knowledge of the game could offer valuable insight, but live commentary requires a different set of skills. He would need to explain complex plays clearly while keeping pace with the action.Travis Kelce's broadcasting opportunities could command $15 millionStill, Kelce could attract serious interest from major networks. Andrew Marchand of The Athletic previously reported that Amazon Prime Video could consider replacing Kirk Herbstreit. Kelce was mentioned as a wild-card candidate, alongside reported priorities Greg Olsen and J.J. Watt.The potential opening on Thursday Night Football could also draw attention if Al Michaels retires. Marchand has reported that Kelce could command $15 million for a studio role alone, highlighting his commercial appeal.Kelce has already shown interest in exploring broadcasting. On Bussin’ With The Boys in July 2025, he said:“I wanna see what calling a game feels like,” Kelce said on the Bussin’ With The Boys podcast in July last year. “Getting in the booth. I’ve always impersonated guys that call the games and stuff like that growing up. I don’t know, I thought it would always be fun to just jump in there. Player names is where I would get \[expletive\] ruined.”His New Heights podcast and 2023 Saturday Night Live appearance have also helped him build a media profile. CBS Sports analyst Nate Burleson even offered to take a pay cut to help bring Kelce to the network.“What I do know is whoever is going after Travis, they’re going to have to back that Brinks truck up, because one, he’s made a ton of money in the league,” Burleson told Front Office Sports. “His lady \[Taylor Swift\] got paper, I’ll be honest. So, he’s not gonna show up for cheap change. And I don’t know if CBS got the budget, but I’d gladly take a pay cut.”For now, Kelce has not committed to a broadcasting career. His next move remains open, and the debate over his potential in the booth is far from settled.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: At a young age, O.J. Simpson dreamed of football greatness, but decades later he became the face of one of America's most infamous murder trials
articles.summary: NFL News: O.J. Simpson's life once seemed like the perfect American success story. A gifted young athlete rose from humble beginnings to become an NFL superstar.
articles.body: O.J. Simpson's life once seemed like the perfect American success story. A gifted young athlete rose from humble beginnings to become an NFL superstar, Hollywood actor and household name. But in 1994, the shocking murders of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ron Goldman changed the course of his life. The football legend soon stood at the centre of a criminal case that would divide the nation and reshape his public legacy.O.J. Simpson's difficult childhood and rise to football fameOrenthal James Simpson was born in San Francisco on July 9, 1947. His early years were far removed from the fame and wealth he would later enjoy. His parents separated when he was young, and his mother raised him and his siblings in the city's Potrero Hill neighbourhood.As a child, Simpson faced health challenges, including rickets, which affected his legs. He also encountered trouble as a teenager. Yet football gave him a direction and a chance to change his circumstances.At Galileo High School, Simpson's talent began to stand out. His academic record initially complicated his path to a major college programme, so he attended City College of San Francisco before transferring to the University of Southern California.At USC, his career took off. Simpson won the Heisman Trophy in 1968, cementing his status as one of college football's brightest stars. The Buffalo Bills selected him in the 1969 NFL Draft, setting the stage for a professional career that would make him a national celebrity.How O.J. Simpson became an NFL legendSimpson's success in the NFL made him one of the defining athletes of his era. His speed, power and ability to break through defensive lines made him a standout running back for the Buffalo Bills. In 1973, he became the first player in NFL history to rush for more than 2,000 yards in a season, reaching 2,003 yards in just 14 games.The achievement earned him the league's Most Valuable Player award and strengthened his place among football's elite. Simpson later played for the San Francisco 49ers before retiring from the NFL in 1979.But football was only one part of his celebrity. Simpson moved into acting, broadcasting and advertising, becoming a familiar face to audiences who did not necessarily follow the sport. His charm and public profile made him a sought-after personality.For years, his image represented success. He had crossed from sports into mainstream entertainment, building a public identity that reached well beyond the football field. That reputation made the events of 1994 all the more startling.The Nicole Brown Simpson and Ron Goldman murders shocked AmericaOn June 12, 1994, Nicole Brown Simpson, O.J. Simpson's former wife, and Ron Goldman were killed outside Nicole's home in the Brentwood area of Los Angeles. The murders quickly became a major national story, and attention soon turned to Simpson.The case took a dramatic turn on June 17, when Simpson failed to surrender to police as expected. He was later seen riding in a white Ford Bronco driven by his friend Al Cowlings. Police followed the vehicle in a slow-speed pursuit through Los Angeles, with television networks broadcasting the scene live.Millions watched as a celebrated sports figure became the focus of a criminal investigation. Simpson eventually surrendered and pleaded not guilty to the murders.The case drew intense attention not only because of Simpson's fame, but also because it raised difficult questions about domestic violence, race, policing and the treatment of evidence. The Los Angeles Police Department's history of racial tension, particularly following the Rodney King case, became a central part of the public debate.What had begun as a double-murder investigation soon became a legal and cultural event that extended far beyond the courtroom.O.J. Simpson's murder trial and the verdict that divided the nationO.J. Simpson's criminal trial began in January 1995 and quickly became known as the "Trial of the Century." Prosecutors argued that forensic evidence connected Simpson to the killings. His defence team challenged the evidence and raised questions about the police investigation, including the conduct of detective Mark Fuhrman.One of the trial's most memorable moments came when Simpson tried on a pair of leather gloves linked to the crime. The gloves appeared not to fit, giving defence attorney Johnnie Cochran a pivotal moment in his closing argument.On October 3, 1995, the jury found Simpson not guilty of the murders of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ron Goldman. The verdict prompted sharply different reactions across the country and intensified debate about race, justice and public trust in law enforcement.The criminal acquittal, however, did not end the legal case. In 1997, a civil jury found Simpson liable for the deaths of Brown Simpson and Goldman and ordered him to pay $33.5 million in damages to their families. The civil verdict used a different legal standard from the criminal trial, and the two outcomes remain central to understanding the case.Simpson continued to deny responsibility for the killings. He died on April 10, 2024, at age 76, after a battle with cancer.The aftermath also followed Simpson into the next chapter of his life. In 2008, he was convicted in a separate Las Vegas case involving armed robbery and kidnapping after a confrontation over sports memorabilia. He served nearly nine years in prison before his release in 2017.That conviction was unrelated to the 1994 murders, but it added another major legal episode to a life already marked by extraordinary highs and devastating controversy.For many, Simpson's story remains a reminder of how quickly public perception can change. His football records and Heisman legacy are part of sports history, while the murders, criminal trial and civil judgment continue to shape how his name is remembered.His life cannot be reduced to a single moment, but neither can the lasting weight of the case be separated from his public legacy. What began with a young boy's dream of football greatness ended as one of the most scrutinised stories in modern American history.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: “I encourage everyone to help support them”: How Patrick Mahomes’ 5-year Special Olympics work and philanthropic efforts with Brittany give back to communities
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes has spent years using his foundation to help young people and communities outside football. His latest Special Olympics effort came wi.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes has spent years using his foundation to help young people and communities outside football. His latest Special Olympics effort came with a simple goal: help athletes get to the biggest stage without worrying about travel and lodging costs.On June 5, 2025, 15 and the Mahomies announced a partnership with Special Olympics Missouri ahead of the 2026 USA Games in Minneapolis. The move also revealed that Mahomes’ support for the organisation had already stretched across five years. Patrick Mahomes turned five years of Special Olympics support into a push for the USA GamesThe Kansas City Chiefs star Patrick Mahomes did not start his Special Olympics involvement in 2025. His foundation had already provided grants to Special Olympics Missouri and its programmes for five years before the new campaign.The June 5 announcement focused on a practical problem. SOMO asked Mahomes’ foundation to identify the three biggest needs facing its athletes. Travel and lodging came out on top, so 15 and the Mahomies directed its new campaign towards those expenses.“We have provided grants for SOMO and its programs for the past five years. With the USA Games coming up, we wanted to help eliminate the financial barriers,” Mahomes said in the June 5, 2025 announcement.The foundation provided seed funding to launch the campaign. Special Olympics Missouri then opened donations at four levels linked to Mahomes’ famous No. 15: $15, $150, $1,500 and $15,000, the “Mahomes Match” level. The campaign ran from June 4 through Dec. 31, 2025, with the money going directly towards travel and lodging for Missouri athletes heading to Minneapolis.Patrick Mahomes also made his personal feelings clear. In the same announcement, he urged people to help the athletes reach their goal.“I encourage everyone to help support and position them to realize their dreams. Let us remove any financial obstacles and allow them to focus on the competition,” Mahomes said. “These athletes are my heroes, and they impress me with their resilience to push through challenges to compete.”That message gave the campaign a personal touch. The foundation was not simply raising money for an event. It was trying to remove a cost that could stand between Missouri athletes and a national competition.Brittany Mahomes and Patrick Mahomes have built a wider giving record around childrenWhile Brittany Mahomes did not take part in the Special Olympics announcement, she has played a role in the couple’s wider charitable work.One of their biggest joint commitments came on Oct. 4, 2023, when 15 and the Mahomies announced a $1.625 million contribution and a multi-year partnership with Boys & Girls Clubs of America. The programme targeted Greater Kansas City, Lubbock, Tyler and Whitehouse, communities with personal links to Patrick and Brittany.The partnership also carried a personal connection for Brittany. Patrick noted that she had attended a Boys & Girls Club as a child. The foundation also pledged $1,500 for every Patrick Mahomes touchdown during the 2023 regular season. Boys & Girls Clubs of East Texas and The Mentoring Alliance planned scholarships for up to 300 children to attend the club each year.“This meaningful partnership will expand opportunities for kids everywhere, and the places that have positively impacted Patrick and me,” Brittany said in the Oct. 4, 2023 announcement. “We are committed to doing all we can to uplift others.”These two efforts show the different ways the Mahomes family has used its foundation. Patrick’s Special Olympics work focused on helping athletes reach Minneapolis, while his joint work with Brittany has also targeted children, clubs and communities that shaped their lives.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Union Jack Classic: Arizona State beat Kansas in first college game at Wembley
articles.summary: Wembley hosted its first American college football game on Saturday, but did the event meet expectations?
articles.body:
It wasn't even gameday in London but the rivalry had already begun.

Fans of the Kansas Jayhawks and Arizona State Sun Devils gathered at a pre-game party in Waterloo on Friday.

Kansas fans shouted their rallying cry "Rock Chalk, Jayhawk", while their rivals replied with "ASU, ASU".

After hosting 42 NFL games since 2007, this was London's introduction to a different kind of American football and a different kind of fandom.

Wembley hosted its first American college football game on Saturday, with 46,523 fans attending the inaugural Union Jack Classic (UJC).

UJC organisers vowed to create an authentic college gameday in London, and they began with tailgate parties.

Fans enjoy food, drink and music for hours before the game, and they are far bigger for college games than in the NFL. One American fan told BBC Sport she prefers the tailgate to the game itself.

The main tailgate at Wembley opened at 10am - seven hours before kick-off - with Kansas City rapper Tech N9ne helping to entertain the crowd.

Arizona State alumni held their own party, with nearly 2,000 fans packed in, while ASU's marching band and cheerleaders performed on stage.

But the wildest party was on Wembley Way, where Fox Sports had an outdoor studio for its live pre-game show.

It was surrounded by fans and the Fox crew kept trying to stoke the rivalry, while the Kansas and ASU bands battled it out on Wembley Way and on the pitch before kick-off.

The pageantry and passion of college football is what makes it different. NFL fans often choose their team, whereas college teams tend to be passed down through families.

"You feel a loyalty to your lineage," said Kansas fan Hannah, who added that college football fans are not just fanatical but "rabid".

BBC Sport spoke to families at Wembley who have had multiple generations attend the same school and alumni who now live all over the US but travel thousands of miles to watch their alma mater.

Current ASU student Sophie said her family "bleeds maroon and gold". Her friend Amelia has ASU merchandise all over the house. She just got a car that's maroon too.

About 15,000 fans travelled from the US for Saturday's game - 9,000 rooting for ASU and 6,000 Kansas.

College games in the US rarely have away fans but, with both teams having a sizable contingent at Wembley, as well as playing at a neutral venue, some visitors said the atmosphere was like a play-off game.

Why UK fans are learning about college football

Fans from 35 countries bought tickets and, as with NFL games in London, they represented several teams, not just those playing.

Neutrals wore NFL jerseys and college jerseys, of bigger schools such as Oklahoma, Miami and Texas. There were even some British university jerseys.

More than 100 universities in the UK have American football teams, and UJC organisers targeted those players, partly because, as students, they often find college football more relatable than the NFL.

They formed partnerships with the British American Football Association, British Universities and Colleges Sport and the Jacksonville Jaguars to establish links with the grassroots game in the UK.

The UJC has helped to train more than 1,050 British coaches and referees this year, some of whom were at Saturday's game.

Cambridge University player Alex said it has been "cool" to learn the stories of Kansas and ASU and he would probably go to more college games in future "if they're teams we can rally behind".

After planning for an attendance of 60,000, Wembley was about half full at 46,523, with some ticketholders moved to the bottom tier to keep the top tier empty.

Although there were some big plays, the game was not as entertaining as anticipated as ASU claimed a 24-17 win that flattered Kansas.

Music acts played throughout the game and there was a light show in the third quarter. It gave UK fans a flavour of college football, but it lacked the pomp and circumstance of regular games in the US.

There were fewer band members and cheerleaders than normal, and the crowd was not as loud as during ASU home games – they averaged 54,000 last season.

Both teams took 105 players (or student-athletes), 90% of which did not have a passport before this trip.

Many fans and members of the coaches' families also visited London for the first time, and ASU head coach Kenny Dillingham said they had "an experience they will remember for the rest of their lives".

Kansas head coach Lance Leipold added that the hospitality was outstanding, while the hotel and practice facility "was a win".

Both teams are part of the Big 12 Conference, whose commissioner Brett Yormark said: "It exceeded my expectations, from the crowd to the logistics to how the local community has embraced us. It's been fantastic, so we want more."

UJC organisers have signed an exclusive multi-year deal with Wembley, and Yormark says other Big 12 colleges are interested in playing in London.

Big 12 teams also played two games in Dublin over the past 13 months, and the conference could expand to another international market.

Yormark said: "There's not a two-week period where I don't get a call to say 'take some of your product to this country or that country', so we're exploring that right now."

He said there will be an announcement about next year's London game "within the next month or two".

That will give UK fans plenty of time to swot up on the next two teams who will make their presence known across the pond.

articles.summary: NFL News: Joe Burrow came out of Cincinnati's Week 1 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with something he did not feel during the game itself. Back tightness cre.
articles.body: Joe Burrow came out of Cincinnati's Week 1 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with something he did not feel during the game itself. Back tightness crept up in the hours after the Bengals' 33-27 win, and by Wednesday, Burrow was listed as limited on the practice report. For a quarterback with his medical history, even a minor entry on the injury report is enough to get fans in Cincinnati holding their breath. Sunday's road trip to Houston now carries a small but real layer of uncertainty around it.Will Joe Burrow play today's game against Texans?Yes, Joe Burrow will play against the Houston Texans today. He dismissed the idea of sitting out for precautionary reasons as flat-out "ridiculous," and made clear he has no intention of missing the game. "I think every game is important," Burrow said at his Wednesday press conference. "I'll do what it takes to be out there. If I'm not having surgery, I'll be out there."Burrow is not entirely sure when he picked up the back issue but says soreness started settling in during the hours after Sunday's game. He was sacked just once but also took a hard shot while scrambling for a first down on a play that eventually led to a touchdown.By Thursday, Burrow was spotted going through his pre-practice throwing routine in full shoulder pads and helmet during the media-accessible portion of practice, which was an encouraging sign pointing toward full participation. So the trajectory has been positive since Wednesday's limited session.Burrow said he is unsure whether he will be able to practice for the full week, but he called it "ridiculous" to think the back issue would force him to sit out Sunday's game.What does Joe Burrow's injury history mean for Bengals fans?This is where the question gets a bit more layered. Burrow's injury history is a sensitive subject in Cincinnati. The franchise quarterback has missed significant time in three of his six NFL seasons, was forced out for most of last season due to a toe injury suffered in Week 2, and is understandably the most valuable player in the Bengals' organization.That's the part that sits in the back of every Bengals fan's mind, no matter how confident Burrow sounds. Last season's turf toe started in Week 2. A wrist injury ended his 2023 campaign in Week 11. The pattern of early-season setbacks is hard to ignore, even if Wednesday's back tightness looks far less serious.Burrow appeared to be in good shape in Sunday's opener, completing 25 of 35 passes for 254 yards and a touchdown, even as he threw a pick-six along the way. The performance itself was not the problem. It was what the body felt afterward.He faces a Texans defense that is still viewed as one of the league's fiercest units, despite allowing a strong performance from Josh Allen in the season opener. Burrow going into that matchup less than 100 percent is not ideal, but based on everything out of Cincinnati this week, he is expected to be on the field when the Bengals and Texans kick off.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: What Travis Kelce sacrificed for years before his $90 million fortune finally started making sense to the world
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce is now worth $90 million. He is married to the world's biggest pop star, holds the NFL record for career playoff receptions, and signed a.
articles.body: Travis Kelce is now worth $90 million. He is married to the world's biggest pop star, holds the NFL record for career playoff receptions, and signed a $100 million podcast deal with Amazon. But none of that happened without cost. Long before any of it, there was a suspended college season, a rookie year lost to injury, and years of building quietly while the world looked elsewhere. The fortune makes sense now. It did not always.What did Travis Kelce sacrifice early in his career to get where he is today?The part of Travis Kelce's story that rarely gets told is how close it came to ending before it began. At the University of Cincinnati, he failed a drug test in 2010 and sat out the entire season. No games. No film. No momentum. For most prospects, that kind of setback finishes them. It nearly finished him.His brother Jason and members of the Cincinnati coaching staff kept him grounded through that year. Kelce returned in 2011, converted fully to tight end, and broke out in 2012 with 45 catches for 722 yards and eight touchdowns. That season saved his draft stock. The Kansas City Chiefs took him 63rd overall in 2013.Then his rookie year disappeared too. A knee injury in the preseason sent him to injured reserve after just one game. Two years of football essentially wiped out before he had ever played a real NFL snap that mattered.He finally broke through in 2014. Sixty-seven catches, 862 yards, five touchdowns. From that point, the production never stopped.How does Travis Kelce actually make his $90 million and where does most of it come from?His NFL salary across 13 seasons accounts for roughly $111 million in career earnings through 2025. His 2026 deal adds another $12 million guaranteed, with incentives that could push it to $15 million. For most athletes, that alone would be the whole story.For Kelce, it is almost a secondary income.His off-field earnings are believed to significantly surpass his on-field salary. Endorsement partners have included Nike, State Farm, McDonald's, Bud Light, T-Mobile, Pfizer, DirecTV, Dick's Sporting Goods, Experian, and Old Spice, among dozens of others. Forbes estimates his annual endorsement income at roughly $30 million.Then there is the podcast. In August 2024, Travis and his brother Jason signed a three-year, $100 million distribution deal with Amazon's Wondery for their show New Heights. The headline figure does not mean $50 million landed in Travis's account directly. Production costs, management fees, and shared revenue reduce the personal take. Still, it remains one of the most significant financial events of his off-field career.His business portfolio also includes equity stakes in Casa Azul Tequila, a stake in Six Flags Entertainment through activist hedge fund JANA Partners, an investment in the Alpine Formula One racing team, and several other consumer brands. The 1587 Prime steakhouse in Kansas City, co-owned with Patrick Mahomes, adds another layer.How much did the Taylor Swift relationship change Travis Kelce's financial value?It changed it more than any contract renegotiation could have. When Swift attended her first Chiefs game in September 2023, Kelce's commercial profile shifted in ways his agents had not modeled. The audience that came with her was global, younger, and largely indifferent to football. They knew Kelce because they knew Taylor.Brands took notice quickly. His endorsement portfolio expanded dramatically, fueled by the visibility that came with his relationship with Swift, which boosted his online presence and marketability across demographics that NFL advertisers had never fully reached before.Travis and Taylor announced their engagement in August 2025 and married in July 2026. Their combined net worth now sits at roughly $1.89 billion, with Taylor accounting for about 95 percent of that figure. The gap matters less than the context. Kelce entered that relationship already wealthy. He left it with a brand worth multiples of what it had been.That is the part the $90 million figure does not fully capture. The number reflects what he earned. It does not reflect what he built. And those are two different things.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: NFL Week 1 gave us some exciting games as we were treated to one of the highest-scoring opening weekends in league history. Where will all 32 teams rank in o...
articles.body:
NFL Week 1 gave us some exciting games as we were treated to one of the highest-scoring opening weekends in league history. Where will all 32 teams rank in our second power rankings of the season? Let's dig in and find out.

Dec 15, 2025; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Miami Dolphins running back De'Von Achane (28) warms up before the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images

#32 Miami Dolphins: This is a rebuilding season, and there will be bumps in the road along the way. Opening day was pretty much what we expected to see. A defense that will struggle to hold opponents off the scoreboard and an offense that will struggle to keep pace.

#31 Cleveland Browns : We knew it was going to be a rough start for the Browns and Deshaun Watson , and they did not disappoint. Things don't get easier this weekend as they travel to Tampa before returning for their home opener in week 3.

#30 Atlanta Falcons : Apparently the starting quarterback position is pretty important. The Falcons' options went from bad to worse to Cooper Rush .

#29 Carolina Panthers : The good news is their offense looked pretty good while scoring 37 points in week 1. The bad news is their defense allowed a record 59 points to the Bears. The silver lining here is that the entire division lost their first game, so they're tied for first in the South.

#28 Tennessee Titans : So much for Robert Saleh's revenge game against the Jets . That game was one of the few that Tennessee will be favored in this season. Not a great start.

#27 Green Bay Packers : Jordan Love and his receivers looked great. The rest of the team choked in the second half and wound up losing to the Carson Wentz-led Vikings by 17. Things will be messy in Green Bay this season unless their offensive line can magically improve.

#26 Indianapolis Colts : Derrick Henry and Lamar Jackson made this defense look like a middle school squad. Daniel Jones looked rusty, but he did manage to survive the game. Better days are likely ahead, but that defense (especially the secondary) needs to improve.

#25 Washington Commanders : They looked outclassed at times, but managed to claw back and make a game of it against the Eagles. This week they travel to Dallas for a second straight division road game.

#24 Las Vegas Raiders : So far, so good in Clint Kubiak's head coaching career. We would like to see them beat somebody tougher than Miami before we get too excited.

Sep 13, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert (10) stands in the pocket against the Arizona Cardinals during the first quarter at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: William Liang-Imagn Images

#23 Los Angeles Chargers: They dropped all the way from #12 in just one week. We were expecting more from the Mike McDaniel-led offense. They can either bounce back with a home win over the Raiders in front of 30,000+ fans wearing Silver and Black, or they could be in for a long season.

#22 Arizona Cardinals: It was just one win, but we had to bump them up 8 spots from last week just based on what their offense is capable of. If this defense can be league average, this team may have something cooking this year.

#21 Tampa Bay Buccaneers : The offense needs to take better care of the ball if this team has aspirations of a winning season. Luckily, they play in the NFC South, so it won't take much to make the postseason.

#20 New Orleans Saints : Congratulations, the Saints are our highest-ranked NFC South team. Of the four teams, they came the closest to winning their game as they gave the Lions quite a scare in Detroit .

#19 New York Jets: It's just one win, but it was an impressive one win. Geno Smith just may keep this offense moving, and the young defensive players all looked very promising. If they can handle the Packers at MetLife this weekend, Jets fans may not even know how to respond.

#18 New York Giants : Two undefeated teams in one city and it's New York, not Los Angeles? This might just be a wacky season. Let's see how this New York team does this Monday Night when they face one of those LA teams when the Giants square off with the Rams .

#17 Pittsburgh Steelers: They won, but it wasn't exactly impressive. Aaron Rodgers has the guile and the experience, but his body is about 2 steps behind. This week, they travel to Foxboro to take on the defending AFC Champs.

Sep 13, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott (4) passes the ball against the New York Giants during the first quarter at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images

#16 Dallas Cowboys: The defense is supposed to be better, but they couldn't get off the field in the second half of the game against the Giants last Sunday night. Dak made just enough mistakes for the game to slip away. They had better take care of Washington in Jerry World this weekend, or it's going to be a rough start to the season in big D.

#15 New England Patriots : It was just one loss, but we don't know if this team can beat good teams when they are fully healthy. This week is a good test when they take on the Steelers at home.

#14 Houston Texans : This defense is supposed to be elite, but they got shredded by Josh Allen . Sure, you can say that it's the great Josh Allen, but that's exactly the guy they need to beat if they have Super Bowl aspirations.

#13 Denver Broncos : One of the biggest fallers of the week, all the way down from #2. They can get back into the top 10 pretty quickly if their defense can show us that last week was just an off night.

#12 Cincinnati Bengals : They took care of business at home against the Bucs. Joe Burrow survived the game with just a few bumps and bruises. As long as he remains healthy, this team has legitimate postseason potential.

#11 Kansas City Chiefs : They're baaaaack! OK, pump the brakes; it was just one game. The fact that Patrick Mahomes had 7 rush attempts, including a 14-yard touchdown, gives us plenty of reason to be optimistic. When you add in the Kenneth Walker performance, we really start to get excited.

Sep 13, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson (18) celebrates after a touchdown during the first half against the Green Bay Packers at U.S. Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Krohn-Imagn Images

#10 Minnesota Vikings: The win was impressive, but this team still hasn't gelled yet. Let's see how they handle the Bears offense this weekend.

#9 San Francisco 49ers : They traveled down under and came away with an opening week victory. The injury to Stribling leaves them with the oldest group of wide receivers in the league. If the injuries pile up, this team won't survive this competitive division.

#8 Detroit Lions : They almost blew the game against the Saints and then had to come back on a short week to face the Bills in Buffalo. This defense looks like it may be a problem for them this season.

#7 Chicago Bears : 59 points? After Ben Johnson told us all that he was going to set records with this offense this year? Oh boy, let's see what they do this week against the Vikings.

#6 Jacksonville Jaguars : OK, it was the Browns, so we can't get too excited. The way Liam Coen had Trevor Lawrence and the offense clicking in the second half of last year has us thinking that this team is for real.

Sep 13, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson (8) throws the ball against the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images

#5 Baltimore Ravens: Every time Lamar Jackson has gotten a new OC, he has won the league's MVP award. After just one game, he looks like he's going for the hat trick.

#4 Los Angeles Rams : We had to ding them after the opening night loss. The Rams will look to get back on track at home this week against the Giants.

#3 Philadelphia Eagles : The offensive line almost stayed healthy for a full game. Almost. Losing Landon Dickerson for at least 4 games is going to hurt, but this team is still one of the best in the NFC.

#2 Buffalo Bills : Josh Allen is on a mission. This year he has healthy weapons around him, and this offense is going to put up a bunch of points every single week.

#1 Seattle Seahawks : If you want to be the best, you've got to beat the best. Right now, this team is the best in the league until somebody comes in and knocks off their crown.

articles.title: How Dianna Russini-Mike Vrabel controversy is making life harder for women building trust in NFL media? ”I wonder who she slept with to get here"
articles.summary: NFL News: The Dianna Russini-Mike Vrabel controversy has stopped being just about two people. Since The Athletic's September review found that Russini's relatio.
articles.body: The Dianna Russini-Mike Vrabel controversy has stopped being just about two people. Since The Athletic's September review found that Russini's relationship with Vrabel created the appearance of a conflict of interest, a bigger, more uncomfortable conversation has been brewing. FOX Sports sideline reporter Jen Hale put it plainly on "The Craig Carton Show" this week. The fallout, she said, isn't staying with the people involved. It is spilling onto every woman who covers this league for a living.How does the Dianna Russini-Mike Vrabel controversy affect other women in NFL media?Hale did not dance around it. When Carton asked whether the controversy had real consequences for other female reporters, she answered without hesitation."It does," Hale said. "It opens the floodgates, absolutely. It makes everything harder, everything tougher."That word, "floodgates," carries a lot of weight. Women covering the NFL have spent years pushing against a baseline suspicion that their access to coaches and players is something other than professional. The Russini-Vrabel story, whatever the full truth of it may be, handed that suspicion a fresh headline.Hale shared a conversation she once had with a younger female reporter who had landed in what Hale described as a similar situation. Her advice was blunt, and by her own admission, it stung a little."I said, 'Look, you need to understand, they are always going to keep their job and you're not. You're easily replaceable, they're not,'" Hale said. "And she thought that that was very dismissive and sexist. And I said, 'I don't agree with it. I'm just telling you the way it works.'"It is a hard thing to say. It is harder still that it needed to be said at all. But Hale is not venting or playing victim. She's describing a professional reality that, fair or not, women in NFL media navigate every single day.Why is building sources in the NFL so different for women than it is for men?Hale used a simple example to show just how uneven the playing field is. She described watching her FOX Sports colleague Mark Schlereth hand a coach his business card during Week 1, telling him to stay in touch. Standard networking. Nothing remarkable about it.But then she asked the obvious question."Can you imagine if I as a female did that?" Hale said. "The rules are different. The engagement rules are different. Developing sources is different."That contrast says more than a long editorial ever could. The same gesture reads completely differently depending on who makes it. And that gap is exactly what gets wider when a story like Russini-Vrabel dominates the sports media news cycle.Hale's larger point lands hardest here. "We have to work so hard to earn our reputation, to not walk in a room and have people think, 'Hmm, I wonder who she slept with to get here,'" she said.Russini resigned from The Athletic after the April photographs surfaced, while Vrabel kept his job as New England's head coach. The Athletic's review, released this month, did not determine whether the relationship was romantic but concluded it violated the outlet's standards by creating a conflict of interest. Russini has defended her reporting throughout.The Patriots opened Week 2 at 0-1. Vrabel remains on the sideline. Russini is no longer at her desk. And female reporters across the country are walking into press boxes this weekend carrying a little more weight than they did before this story broke.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: How Aaron Rodgers turned the darkest chapter of his career into the setup for one of the most emotionally charged farewell seasons in pro football history
articles.summary: NFL News: Four snaps. That's all Aaron Rodgers got in New York. On the fourth play of his Jets debut in September 2023, he went down with a torn Achilles, and a.
articles.body: Four snaps. That's all Aaron Rodgers got in New York. On the fourth play of his Jets debut in September 2023, he went down with a torn Achilles, and a lot of people assumed that was it. A gut-punch exit for a four-time MVP who'd given 18 years to Green Bay, then chased one more shot in a new city. Instead, Rodgers rehabbed, returned for a difficult 2024 in New York, moved on to Pittsburgh, helped the Steelers to a 10-6 record in 2025, and is now back for one final season. At 42, his parting statement isn't a quiet goodbye.Why did Aaron Rodgers decide to play one more season in 2026?At training camp in Latrobe, Aaron Rodgers shut down any lingering retirement ambiguity fast. "Zero debate. Zero," he told reporters when asked if 2026 was truly it. Coming from a man who spent the better part of a decade in quarterback limbo, first with the Packers, then the Jets, then Pittsburgh, that kind of certainty means something.The honest version of how he got here is pretty human. Rodgers thought 2025 might be it. Then Mike Tomlin stepped down after 19 seasons, the Steelers hired Mike McCarthy, and Rodgers had a conversation with his wife. She told him he could do one more year. So he signed a one-year deal worth up to $25 million and reported to his 22nd NFL training camp. That's the story. No grand declaration, just a man who wasn't quite done and had enough reason to come back.The McCarthy factor is real. Rodgers played under him for 13 seasons in Green Bay. Their working relationship had enough friction to fill a book, but also enough shared success to make a reunion meaningful. "I spent 13 years in his offense," Rodgers said. "It's stuff that we used to run." McCarthy, for his part, was open about what this moment means. "Every day," he said when asked if the significance of coaching Rodgers in his final season is lost on him. It clearly isn't.What made Aaron Rodgers' time with the Jets so damaging to his legacy?The Jets chapter is hard to look back on cleanly. The 2023 trade was supposed to end New York's 13-year playoff drought. The hype was enormous. Rodgers was running out of the tunnel at MetLife Stadium on a Monday night with 80,000 people going out of their minds, and four plays later, he was on the turf, Achilles gone.He described it simply: "a lot of sadness, a lot of tears." He had surgery, attacked his rehab, and came back for 2024. The Jets finished 5-12 with Rodgers throwing 29 touchdown passes and 11 interceptions. The new regime released him. He was "shocked" at how the new brass handled his departure. Two years, one game's worth of actual production, and a team no closer to relevance. That's a brutal stretch for anyone, let alone a quarterback of Rodgers' standing.But the Achilles recovery is genuinely remarkable. He was 39 when it happened, 40 when he returned. Torn Achilles injuries at that age almost always end things. His didn't. And while his first full Jets season was underwhelming by his standards, he held up physically, showed more mobility late in the year, and walked out of New York with his arm still working. Pittsburgh took the bet.What is at stake for Aaron Rodgers in his final NFL season with the Steelers?The Hall of Fame case is not in question. Four-time NFL MVP, 22 seasons. He enters 2026 ranked in the top seven in most major quarterback categories. Only Peyton Manning has won more MVP awards. That part is settled. What this final year is really about is something harder to measure.Still, there's a compelling subplot. The Steelers and Packers are not on each other's 2026 regular season schedule. The only place those two franchises could meet is the Super Bowl. That's a long shot by anyone's math, but it's the kind of story the NFL seems to write sometimes.Rodgers has already been building chemistry with receivers like DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. on an offseason ranch trip. Metcalf hinted he wasn't ruling out a late change of heart from Rodgers if the season goes well. "People just say things at the beginning of the year, not knowing how a year could go," Metcalf said. Rodgers heard it and wasn't bothered. He knows how he wants this to end.He came back from a torn Achilles at 40. He survived two fractured years in New York. He found a home in Pittsburgh with the coach who helped build his prime. Now 42, Rodgers isn't limping toward the finish line. He's had worse situations. He's used to doing things the hard way.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany celebrate a love story that began years before his Super Bowl success
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes may have built his name through record-breaking performances and Super Bowl victories, but one of the most meaningful parts of his jou.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes may have built his name through record-breaking performances and Super Bowl victories, but one of the most meaningful parts of his journey began long before the NFL spotlight. His relationship with Brittany Mahomes has weathered career changes, personal milestones and the pressure of professional football. From their teenage years in Texas to raising three children, their story has grown alongside Patrick's rise to NFL stardom.Patrick and Brittany Mahomes' relationship began before NFL fameThe Mahomes love story started in 2012 at Whitehouse High School in Texas. At the time, neither teenager knew how dramatically their lives would change. They shared a love for sports, but their ambitions took different routes.Patrick played football, baseball and basketball during his school years. Brittany, meanwhile, focused on soccer and built her own athletic career. Their relationship continued through college, even as they attended different universities.Patrick enrolled at Texas Tech, where he initially pursued both football and baseball. His decision to focus on football eventually opened the door to the NFL. The Kansas City Chiefs selected him with the 10th overall pick in the 2017 NFL Draft.Brittany also pursued her sporting ambitions beyond college. She played professional soccer in Iceland before turning her attention to fitness and business. Her career later expanded into the NWSL, where she became part of the ownership group behind the Kansas City Current.Their paths show that the Mahomes partnership has never been limited to Patrick's football career. Both built their own professional identities while maintaining a relationship that began in their teens.Patrick's NFL success soon brought a new chapter. He became Kansas City's starting quarterback in 2018 and won the league's MVP award that season. The Chiefs captured their first Super Bowl title of his career after the 2019 season, defeating the San Francisco 49ers in Super Bowl LIV.By then, Brittany had witnessed the early stages of a career that would transform their lives.Brittany Mahomes and Patrick build a family amid Super Bowl gloryIn September 2020, Patrick proposed to Brittany at Arrowhead Stadium following the Chiefs' Super Bowl ring ceremony. The setting carried special meaning, as the stadium had become central to Patrick's professional journey.Their first child, Sterling Skye, arrived in February 2021. The couple married in Maui, Hawaii, on March 12, 2022, with their daughter playing a special role in the ceremony.Family life soon became an even bigger part of their story. Their son, Patrick "Bronze" Lavon Mahomes III, was born in November 2022, followed by their youngest daughter, Golden Raye, in January 2025.As their family grew, so did Patrick's collection of NFL honours. The Chiefs defeated the Philadelphia Eagles in Super Bowl LVII after the 2022 season. They then beat the 49ers in Super Bowl LVIII, earning Patrick his third championship.Brittany and their children joined him for the celebrations, becoming familiar faces during some of Kansas City's biggest moments.However, their journey has also included difficult stretches. Patrick's serious knee injury late in the 2025 season tested his recovery and kept him away from the field. Brittany remained part of his support system as he worked towards returning to football.That return came on September 14, 2026, when Patrick led the Chiefs against the Denver Broncos in the season opener. Kansas City won 31-10, and Brittany shared a kiss with him on the sideline after his comeback.The moment offered a glimpse into a relationship that has lasted through much more than championship celebrations. articles.title: Shedeur Sanders Starting, Deshaun Watson Benching Eyed After Browns vs. Bucs, New NFL Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns are expected to reexamine their quarterback situation after their Week 2 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, according to Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns are expected to reexamine their quarterback situation after their Week 2 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, according to Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network.

"While no firm decision has been made for Week 3, the belief is that the first two games would serve as a natural evaluation point," Rapoport said. "In other words, the Browns could use the return to Cleveland for their Week 3 home opener and a two-game sample size as the impetus for a quarterback change."

Deshaun Watson will start Sunday for the second straight week. Should the Browns go in a different direction, Shedeur Sanders would be the next man up.

A quarterback change felt inevitable as soon as Cleveland announced Watson as the starter, and the team's 34-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars only reinforced the idea.

Watson went 16-of-22 for 205 yards, one touchdown and an interception, and he was sacked five times.

Since earning his last Pro Bowl nod in 2020, the 31-year-old missed two full seasons. When he has played, he has looked much worse in comparison to his peak with the Houston Texans.

Watson has averaged 178.5 yards per contest and posted an 81.3 passer rating in his 20 starts on the Browns. His support among Cleveland fans has totally eroded as well.

Maybe Watson lights it up against the Buccaneers and presents his team with a dilemma. Assuming that doesn't happen, it will be harder to justify keeping him QB1.

Sanders didn't excel as a rookie. Across the Browns' final seven games, he threw for 1,353 yards, seven touchdowns and nine interceptions while completing 59.2 percent of his passes.

But Sanders is also the closest thing Cleveland has to a long-term solution under center, and he showed enough in 2025 to warrant another extended look.

The Browns have two first-round picks in the 2027 NFL draft , and their own could fall within the top five. They need to have a firm idea on Sanders' talent level ahead of the draft so they know whether they should target a quarterback early on Day 1.

Moving Sanders up the depth chart as early as Week 3 would help to fulfill that objective.

articles.title: Tua Tagovailoa Release Status, Michael Penix Jr.'s Injury Return Addressed in New Falcons Rumors
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons aren't expected to part ways with veteran quarterback Tua Tagovailoa once their QB room is fully healthy, according to ESPN's Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons aren't expected to part ways with veteran quarterback Tua Tagovailoa once their QB room is fully healthy, according to ESPN's Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter .

The insiders reported Tagovailoa's tenure "has become a topic for discussion," but he isn't going anywhere anytime soon.

Tagovailoa is doubtful for Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers because of an oblique injury. Michael Penix Jr., meanwhile, is out altogether as he continues working his way back from a partially torn ACL.

Rapoport and Schefter reported Penix could be cleared to play the Green Bay Packers in Week 3.

Penix said this week he's "close" to a return.

"I know I've been saying that, but there's just a couple of technical things that I want to hit, some goals that I have that I want to achieve before I do stuff out on that field," he said. "But I do feel really good, and we're taking strides each and every day."

Cooper Rush is in line to start Sunday for the second straight week. He went 12-of-22 for 143 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in a 20-13 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Needless to say, the Falcons would benefit from having at least one of Penix or Tagovailoa available. In the case of the latter, Atlanta could have a motivation beyond trying to win games.

Tagovailoa counts for just $1.2 million against the salary cap this season and will be a free agent in 2027. Rapoport and Schefter presented a scenario where he regains some of his old form and becomes a valuable trade asset.

Assuming they're pretty much out of the playoff race in another month, flipping the 2023 Pro Bowler for a draft pick would be a nice piece of business for the Falcons.

If Atlanta instead believes it can contend for a postseason place, then it can ill afford to go much longer with Rush as QB1.

articles.body: Travis Kelce's success with the Kansas City Chiefs has helped him build a real estate portfolio that stretches beyond the football field. From a luxury mansion in a gated Kansas City community to a Florida condo shared with his family, the NFL star has invested in properties that reflect his career and personal roots. His real estate journey also includes a major upgrade from his earlier Kansas City home.Travis Kelce's $6 million Kansas City mansion is his primary residenceFor Kelce, Kansas City has become much more than the place where he built his NFL career. It is also where he has established his home base.The Chiefs tight end's primary residence is a $6 million mansion in a gated community near Kansas City, according to Hello Magazine. The property offers a level of privacy and luxury that suits a player whose career has brought him considerable fame.However, this wasn't always Kelce's standard of living. Before moving into the upscale estate, he owned a seven-bedroom home in Kansas City's Briarcliff West neighbourhood. He purchased that property in 2019 for $995,000.The earlier house marked an important stage in his career. Kelce had already established himself as one of the NFL's leading tight ends, but his real estate choices would later reflect his growing financial success.His move to a more expensive home also highlights how his life has changed since entering the league. With multiple seasons of success in Kansas City, Kelce has built a strong connection to the city, making it a natural choice for his primary residence.The $6 million mansion remains the standout property associated with his personal real estate portfolio. Still, his property interests extend beyond Missouri.Travis Kelce's Florida condo reflects his family's real estate tiesKelce's connection to Florida comes through a property owned jointly with members of his family. The NFL star co-owns a condo in the Baldwin Park area of Orlando with his mother, Donna Kelce, and brother, Jason Kelce.The property has a family connection that goes beyond its market value. Donna, who is a full-time Florida resident, purchased the condo in May 2019 for $355,000.Property records indicate that nearly the entire Kelce family is included on the deed. articles.title: How one Indiana city went from skeptical to serious contender for Bears' new stadium
articles.summary: Hammond, Indiana, Mayor Thomas McDermott Jr. said the Chicago Bears stadium project is "in the red zone" as bipartisan cooperation fuels Indiana's bid.
articles.body: When the Chicago Bears kick off against the Minnesota Vikings for their 2026 home opener on Sunday, it will mark the start of their 55th season at Soldier Field. It also may be the last. Hammond, Indiana, certainly hopes it is. The Bears announced in June that they were moving forward with stadium development plans across state lines in Hammond, Indiana. This isn’t the first time the Bears have talked about moving to Indiana, as there were discussions in the late 1990s, but none were serious. Now? The discussions are as serious as Ben Johnson saying he wants the Bears to have the highest-scoring offense in NFL history. Hammond Mayor Thomas McDermott Jr. said that while the city has been preparing for this, even he didn’t think the work would eventually lead to Hammond potentially becoming the next home of the Bears. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "We did a lot of things in Hammond and in Indiana to prepare us for this day," McDermott told OutKick in a recent interview. "But you know, I'd be lying to you if I told you I thought that when we were doing this, I thought we'd be the future home of the Chicago Bears." How Hammond Prepared for This The Bears completed their review of the Lost Marsh site in Hammond while also doing their due diligence on the Lake Terminal site. McDermott said those potential sites for a stadium came to be through efforts to clean up the area. "The site that we're talking about right now, if you were looking at it when I first took over, it was I don't think the Bears would have even thought it was possible to locate a stadium there because there was so many different landowners. it was underutilized and it was just old-fashioned, old thinking," McDermott said. "For the first two or three terms, in cooperation with the state government, we started assembling dozens and dozens of acres and we got it to where we have about 300 acres available." But even throughout the process of assembling the acreage, it was never done with the thought the it could one day be the home of the Bears. "I'll be honest with you, never in a million years did I think that we'd one day be the home—the future home of the Chicago Bears. We were just doing it to clean up and hoping that good things would happen and improve the quality of life," McDermott said. However, acquiring and developing land wasn’t the only thing Hammond did to prepare for the Bears. The state of Indiana has more favorable property tax caps than Illinois, which McDermott said was of interest to the Bears. "Another thing that Indiana did to prepare for this day was there's a gap from one side of the state line to the other in what it costs to run a household, what it costs to run a business, and in Indiana, we enshrine tax caps, property tax caps, into our constitution. And one of the buzzwords of this whole ordeal with the Bears is property tax certainty, which is something the Bears are interested in, and they can't get property tax certainty in Illinois," McDermott said. "And certainly in year zero and for the next 30 years, they certainly can't get property tax certainty. And in Indiana, ours are enshrined in our constitution. You can't pay over 1%, 2% or 3% depending on your classification." Heather Ennis, president and CEO of the Northwest Indiana Forum, told OutKick in a recent interview that Northwest Indiana has seen billions of dollars invested in the region, not including any potential deal with the Bears. "We're a $52 billion regional economy and we're seeing in the last 10 months over $30 billion of investment committed to the region, and that doesn't even include any of the Bears conversation. So we're really seeing people be bullish on Northwest Indiana and the opportunities that are coming to the region," Ennis told OutKick. Another thing working in Hammond’s favor? Complete cooperation across the board. WWE NXT STAR TALKS CHICAGO BEARS' POSSIBLE MOVE TO INDIANA: 'WHAT THE F?' McDermott said he has never seen more bipartisan cooperation in his 23 years than he has during the Bears discussions. "I'm in my sixth term and I've never seen the coordination across federal, state, bipartisan, Republican and Democratic lines, everybody working in lockstep. And I mean from the U.S. senators in Indiana, both of them are working on this project. The congressman in Indiana who's a Democrat, both U.S. senators are Republicans, the governor is a Republican and I'm a Democrat. And you wouldn't know it at all when you're looking at everybody working so hard on this project," McDermott said "Governor Braun has been a great leader for Indiana. He is helping Hammond out tremendously. And this is a Democratic city that probably didn’t vote for Governor Braun for governor. So the bipartisanship, the federal partnerships that we have with the state partnerships, you need all that. And quite frankly, we started off on one location in Hammond and sort of changed course a couple months ago and nothing changed. We just shifted modes up here. And I think that impressed the - it was literally a gear shift and we just rolled right with it and they're the customer." "If this is what the Bears want us to look at, no problem, sir. And we get to work. And it's been very business friendly. I think the Bears would tell you they're very impressed with the bipartisanship and the total cooperation they've received from Indiana." Why a Move Feels Real This is not the first time the Bears have considered moving to Indiana. In the late 1990s, they considered moving to Gary, Indiana. But it didn’t work out, which is why McDermott, among many others, was skeptical that the Bears were serious about making a move this time around. "I'll be honest with you, I started off skeptical. I really did because we've been through this drill before in Northwest Indiana in the '90s, a similar type of situation with the Bears. The location was supposed to be the city of Gary at the time and that never panned out. And there was a lot of skepticism in Northwest Indiana that the Bears were never serious in the '90s and they're probably not serious now," McDermott said. I like to close deals. So, as a mayor, even if you think there's not much of a possibility, you're still going to work your tail off to try to make it happen. And that's the approach I took to it." McDermott said he was brought in last year around the holidays but that Gov. Mike Braun and the speaker of the House were involved long before he was. McDermott said he had to sign nondisclosure agreements to keep things quiet. For McDermott, things didn’t feel real until he got a call from a big company that he declined to identify about the potential acquisition of its property. "When I started to finally feel like this was the real deal, I remember there was a big company in my city," McDermott said. "But a big company called my office and it panicked because they got calls from the state of Indiana about their property being acquired. And that's when I was like, 'Okay.’" "It was a big company and they were like, 'Mayor, do you know what's going on? Why is the state of Indiana interested in buying our property?' And we couldn't tell them why, but there were a lot of high fives in City Hall that day because that's when it hit me. Wow, this isn't the 1990s. This is a totally different ordeal." As for Soldier Field, the Bears’ lease runs through 2033, but they can pay a fee to break the lease early. Soldier Field is about 40 miles south of Halas Hall — the team’s headquarters in Lake Forest — and Hammond is about 20 miles south of the team’s lakefront stadium. Indiana House Speaker Todd Huston was the lead House sponsor of Senate Bill 27, which passed with ease. The bill created a funding mechanism for the Northwest Indiana Stadium Authority to build a future stadium in the state. Huston said the Bears moving to Indiana would create opportunities that would last for generations. "This project would be a transformational opportunity for Northwest Indiana. It would deliver lasting benefits across the region and our entire state, building on a foundation that’s already been put in place for the last two decades. Northwest Indiana is experiencing tremendous growth and potential, and an investment of this scale would take that to another level — bringing new jobs and businesses, attracting visitors and residents, and creating opportunities that will benefit Hoosiers for generations," Huston told OutKick in a statement. "Indiana has created an environment that keeps costs low for businesses and families, attracts investment, supports job growth and expands opportunity. When the potential of this project presented itself, state and local leaders recognized its potential and moved quickly. That combination of a low-cost, forward-looking environment and a willingness to get things done is what continues to attract businesses, investment and people to Indiana." ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH.
