Building the infrastructure Becoming the new home of a professional football team means a lot more than just building a stadium and then calling it a day. The city also needs to have requisite infrastructure to harbor tens of thousands of fans, highways and roads for them to travel on. With Hammond on the southern tip of Lake Michigan, McDermott said the utility infrastructure is already well developed. "We have a lot of big businesses here. We have industrial businesses here. We have a data center here. We have big users of energy and our infrastructure. Hammond's located just to the south of the tip of Lake Michigan. So, all of the infrastructure, the utilities, the highways, the rail lines go through Hammond. And in a project like this, the fact that the utility infrastructure is already so built up because we're the southern tip of Lake Michigan is helping us tremendously when we're looking at bringing in a stadium because the stadium needs heavy infrastructure," McDermott said. McDermott said Arlington Heights, Illinois, about 30 miles northwest of Chicago and another location the Bears are considering, faces a challenge in terms of infrastructure, while Hammond doesn’t have that same issue. While Hammond doesn’t face that same issue, McDermott said the area does need significant highway, interstate and road infrastructure improvements, but it already has a good blueprint. "Although we're going to need a massive infusion of highway and off-interstate and road infrastructure improvements, there's $600 million built into this deal for infrastructure improvements around the proposed footprint of the stadium. We already have a good blueprint and it's only going to get bigger and better," McDermott said. Ennis said Indiana has all the infrastructure needed to bring a project like this to fruition, calling Indiana "the crossroads of America." "We are the region that built America. Over 25% of the nation's steel is built here and in our region, and so we have all of the infrastructure to be able to bring a project like this to fruition. We've got great highway infrastructure connectivity to Chicago. We've double tracked the commuter rail line and have an extension of that commuter rail line to extend down further into Lake County," Ennis said. "We are truly part of the Chicago metro area, and so that great base of infrastructure that is already here with the beautiful waterfront, the great highway infrastructure, the commuter rail system. There definitely will need to be improvements made to continue to connect these sites to the opportunities that already exist, but other regions around the country drool over the infrastructure that we have here in Northwest Indiana." For fans who are concerned about the stadium moving from Soldier Field to Hammond, McDermott admitted it’s easier to get to Soldier Field but said there are many ways to commute to Indiana. "If you're in downtown Chicago, I understand that it was a lot easier to go to Soldier Field, but we are connected by highway. We're connected by water during certain times of year and by rail. It's far easier to get to Hammond and quicker than it would be to get to Arlington Heights," McDermott said. "And the Bears could build a heck of a lot more stadium in Indiana than they could in Illinois right now because of the financial situation in Indiana versus Illinois. So, if you're a true fan of the Chicago Bears, I think we're going to have a better fan experience in Indiana. I think the team's going to be better in Indiana." SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER New City, Same Name McDermott made it clear: The Chicago Bears will remain the Chicago Bears. A name change was never discussed. "Not even once. There is nothing. Listen, there's some Hammond Bears stuff going around Northwest Indiana, but I'm sure the Bears didn't authorize it. I just want you to know that was never—it's more of a local pride thing," McDermott said. "Everybody knows the Chicago Bears are the Chicago Bears. That's never been broached by the state government or by the city government. The Chicago Bears are an icon, and there's no way we'd ever ask them to change their name." The Bears themselves have echoed the same sentiment. "We will be the Chicago Bears whether we’re in Arlington or whether we’re in Hammond," Bears chairman George McCaskey said in August. McDermott also made it clear that while many people assume Indiana residents are automatically Indianapolis Colts fans, Northwest Indiana is Bears country. "I know we're in Indiana. I know everybody thinks just because of our address in Indiana that we're Colts fans. That is not the case. In Northwest Indiana, it's the Bears, and probably the Packers are probably the second most liked team. The Colts are probably third in the region where we're talking about right now, but it's Bears country. So, like I said, I want the Bears to be good this year because everybody's happy when the Bears are good," McDermott said. Where Do Negotiations Currently Stand? The Bears scored 59 points in their Week 1 win against the Carolina Panthers, dominating in the red zone. Using an analogy in which a touchdown means the Bears are officially moving to Hammond, McDermott said the ball is currently in the red zone. "We're in the red zone for sure. So, where are we in the red zone? I think the only people that could answer that is Mr. McCaskey and Kevin Warren. But I definitely think we're in the red zone and there's a lot of work going on, and it's hard to punch the ball into the end zone, and that's where we are right now," McDermott said. "When you're in the red zone, the defense is tightened up and everybody's shoved into a little box and it's even harder to score. I think that's where we are right now, but we're going to punch it in." McDermott said the ball is in the hands of McCaskey and Bears President Kevin Warren and that things are out of his control. "The ball is 100% in their court. So, I try not to make promises. I realize this is not in my control. I hope that it's done sooner. I hope that the Bears choose Hammond and we start moving forward, and that's all it is really. It's hoping," McDermott said. "But, you know, the Bears are going to do it when they're comfortable, and if they're going to invest billions of dollars into a piece of property, they got to be very comfortable that what they're doing is the right thing, and that's what they're doing and I don't blame them, you know?" "The Bears would—we would be lucky to have the Bears come here, but they would be just as lucky to locate here because we really have our act together and our communities are really working in lockstep to make those investments happen. Working together with the state, you know, across the entire platform to really make things happen," Ennis said. As a Bears fan, McDermott doesn’t want to disrupt the team and bug McCaskey or Warren too much. If McCaskey and Warren are anything like the Bears’ offense, they might make it to the end zone sooner rather than later and make Indiana the team’s new home. articles.title: New Broncos Rumors on Davis Webb's Status After NFL Exec Talks 'Very Messy' Outlook with Sean Payton
articles.summary: After a lackluster Week 1 performance, Davis Webb's status as offensive play-caller for the Denver Broncos already appears to be on some thin ice from the outside looking in.
articles.body:
After a lackluster Week 1 performance, Davis Webb's status as offensive play-caller for the Denver Broncos already appears to be on some thin ice from the outside looking in.

The Athletic's Jonathan Jones noted on Saturday that one executive from a rival AFC club explained things could get "very messy" between Webb and head coach Sean Payton if the Broncos have a slow start on Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars:

"I think Sean's play calling last year was unbelievable. He is such an elite play caller. Davis is a good dude, but he's 31 and never called plays before. That's going to be an interesting situation. They have a helluva schedule. They have a tough one against Jacksonville. If they come out of the gates slowly, it's gonna be hard for Sean to stick with this. That would get very messy."

However, ESPN's Adam Schefte r, citing sources, reported on Sunday morning that the Broncos have a "high level of confidence and comfort" in Webb.

One of the most surprising moves of the NFL offseason was Payton announcing in February that he was ceding play-calling duties for the offense to Webb.

The decision came as Webb was generating a lot of interest as a head coaching candidate. He was reportedly viewed as a "strong" option for the Las Vegas Raiders, and he interviewed with the Buffalo Bills and Baltimore Ravens.

Webb wound up withdrawing his name from consideration for the Raiders job. The 31-year-old has only been coaching since the 2023 season when he was hired by Payton to join Denver's staff. He was the quarterbacks coach for three seasons, and added the title of offensive pass game coordinator in 2025.

Webb had no prior play-calling experience before being named Broncos offensive coordinator in February. It also marked the first time in Payton's head-coaching career dating back to his first season with the New Orleans Saints in 2006 that he wasn't calling plays for the offense.

The entirety of Denver's performance in a 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 1 was a disappointment, but the offense putting up 176 yards and nine first downs led to a lot of scrutiny around the play-calling.

Even though Payton came to Webb's defense , it's hard to envision a head coach who is as hands-on as Payton has been throughout his career not taking control if he thinks things are spiraling in the wrong direction.

Sunday's game against a Jaguars defense that gave Denver plenty of problems in their Week 16 matchup last season could go a long way toward determining if Webb holds onto his job or if Payton steps back in.

articles.title: New Joey Porter Jr. Injury Update, Timeline for Return Revealed amid Steelers Trade Rumors
articles.summary: With his contract situation looming, Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. could be in line to make his season debut in Week 3 against the Cincinnati Bengals.
articles.body:
With his contract situation looming, Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. could be in line to make his season debut in Week 3 against the Cincinnati Bengals.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Sunday the Steelers are "planning" for him to "potentially return" against their AFC North rivals, although "whether or not Porter actually does return is a bit more ambiguous and is connected to the star cornerback's back injury and conditioning level."

A source told Schefter that Porter's back "flared up when he's tried to go full speed, and they haven't been able to get it where it needs to be."

This comes after Tom Pelissero of The Ringer reported the Steelers do not plan on breaking their "longstanding organizational policy by resuming contract negotiations in-season with Porter," which means "nobody should rule out the possibility Porter's next game is in another uniform."

What's more, Jonathan Jones of The Athletic reported the cornerback, who "wants a long-term contract," could be traded as a result with one league source saying, "a trade is not out of the question on this stuff."

Pittsburgh and Porter were unable to come to terms on a contract extension this offseason, meaning he is in the final year of his deal that is paying him $3.9 million in base salary in 2026.

Just this offseason, Devon Witherspoon and the Seattle Seahawks agreed to a four-year, $132 million extension that temporarily made him the highest-paid cornerback in the league before the New England Patriots and Christian Gonzalez topped that with a four-year, $135 million extension .

With so much high-profile movement at the cornerback position this offseason, Porter wanted to be next in line.

But the Steelers haven't budged, and now his back is a concern as well as he is set to miss Sunday's game against the Patriots after sitting out the season opener against the Atlanta Falcons as well.

Schefter added that "the two sides haven't gotten close to an agreement, which has brought the possibility of a trade into play." ESPN's Brooke Pryor and Jeremy Fowler previously reported some believed there was "a fracture in the relationship" between player and team.

Still, potential suitors will likely want to see him on the field sooner rather than later so they know he can play at a high level if they are going to give up draft-pick compensation or anything else in the move.

Perhaps that comes when the Steelers face the Bengals and he goes against Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins on the outside.

At his best, Porter is one of the best young cornerbacks in the league.

The 26-year-old tallied 14 passes defended last season and hasn't given up a touchdown in man-to-man coverage since he was a rookie during the 2023 season. His presence can transform a defense and make life easier for his teammates by shutting down a top option in the aerial attack, but the Steelers will have to wait at least a week to see that this season.

articles.title: Trey Hendrickson 'Broke a Finger Into Several Pieces' in Ravens Debut, Latest Injury Buzz for Week 2
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens pass-rusher Trey Hendrickson will reportedly be on the field for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints despite suffering a setback in his team's season-opening win over the Indianapolis Colts.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens pass-rusher Trey Hendrickson will reportedly be on the field for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints despite suffering a setback in his team's season-opening win over the Indianapolis Colts.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Sunday that Hendrickson "broke a finger into several pieces this week" but will still play with a cast on his hand to protect the injury.

Hendrickson missed practice on Wednesday and Thursday before he was limited Friday. That left his official status as questionable for Sunday's game, but he will be on the field anchoring Baltimore's pass-rush.

That pass-rush was excellent for stretches of the Week 1 win over the Colts, as the Ravens tallied two sacks and nine quarterback hits against Daniel Jones. Hendrickson himself did not post a quarterback hit or sack, but he drew additional attention from the offensive line at times and opened up more favorable blitzing lanes for his teammates.

Tavius Robinson in particular stood out with four quarterback hits and one sack.

While Hendrickson was limited to four games last season with the Cincinnati Bengals, he led the NFL with 17.5 sacks in 2024 when he appeared in all 17 games. He also made his fourth consecutive Pro Bowl and was named to the First Team All-Pro as a result.

That was the pass-rusher the Ravens envisioned adding when they brought in Hendrickson after their trade for Maxx Crosby was nullified . And he will look to get his first sack with the Ravens on Sunday despite the cast on his hand.

New Orleans is coming off a 31-30 overtime loss to the Detroit Lions in its season opener, and quarterback Tyler Shough was sacked five times in defeat. Whether Baltimore can generate that type of pressure could make the difference in the game, as Shough also threw for 410 yards and looked more comfortable as the game progressed.

In fact, the Saints forced overtime despite falling behind 21-0 in the third quarter.

If Hendrickson and Co. can make life difficult on Shough, they could avoid some of the late-game drama the Lions had to survive in Week 1.

articles.title: "You're a sore loser": Tom Brady and Logan Paul's controversial feud turns worse as he makes controversial comments against the NFL legend
articles.summary: NFL News: Tom Brady, the seven time Super Bowl champion, is easily one of the legendary athletes that the world has ever seen. While the New England Patriots’ l.
articles.body: Tom Brady, the seven time Super Bowl champion, is easily one of the legendary athletes that the world has ever seen. articles.body: Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza is back in the spotlight heading into Sunday's Week 2 divisional clash against the Los Angeles Chargers. With backup Aidan O'Connell ruled out for personal reasons, the Raiders enter today's game with only two quarterbacks available, putting Mendoza squarely in the backup role. It is not just a depth chart shuffle -- it raises a legitimate question about how soon the first overall pick could see meaningful action.Will Fernando Mendoza start today's game against Chargers?No, Fernando Mendoza will not start today's game against the Chargers. Kirk Cousins remains the Raiders' starter heading into Sunday's divisional matchup at Allegiant Stadium. Mendoza is listed as the backup after O'Connell was ruled out for personal reasons, meaning the rookie is now one play away from getting his first regular-season reps.That said, the question of how long Cousins holds onto the job is louder this week than it was seven days ago. In Week 1 against the Dolphins, Cousins completed just one of seven passes on throws 10 or more yards downfield, also throwing two interceptions on those attempts. For a 38-year-old signed to bridge the gap to the franchise's future, those are numbers that raise eyebrows quickly.The Raiders selected Mendoza with the top pick this past draft, pairing him with Cousins and new head coach Klint Kubiak -- who just won a Super Bowl as Seattle's offensive coordinator. The plan was always to ease the rookie in, not throw him into the fire in September. But if Cousins cannot push the ball past the sticks consistently against stiffer competition, that timeline could move up fast.Mendoza stood on the sideline during last week's season opener, watching as Las Vegas dominated a Dolphins side that looks like a serious 2027 draft lottery contender. The win was convincing, but the opponent made it hard to draw too many conclusions about Cousins' arm.What happens if Kirk Cousins struggles against the Chargers today?The calls for Mendoza will get louder. That is just the reality when you draft a player first overall and the starter's most glaring weakness is showing up on tape in back-to-back weeks.O'Connell's absence strips away the experienced safety net behind Cousins. The former Purdue product has appeared in 21 games across his career, completing 62 percent of his passes for 3,932 yards and 20 touchdowns. He brought real depth and emergency experience to this room. Without him today, Mendoza is the only option if Cousins goes down or gets pulled.The Chargers, meanwhile, are playing this one desperate. They dropped Week 1 and cannot afford an 0-2 hole in the division. Justin Herbert and Ladd McConkey give Los Angeles real weapons, and defensive coordinator Chris O'Leary is likely to load the box and dare Cousins to beat them downfield -- exactly the area where he struggled most against Miami.If that pressure piles up and the passing game stalls again, the conversation around Mendoza's debut will shift from "eventually" to "now."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2020, a Kansas City man traded for 100 Patrick Mahomes rookie cards; the forgotten haul was later valued at around $7,000, helping his family through a crisis
articles.summary: NFL News: A box of 100 Patrick Mahomes rookie cards once looked like little more than a mystery find at a thrift store. In 2020, Trevor Hayes ended up with the .
articles.body: A box of 100 Patrick Mahomes rookie cards once looked like little more than a mystery find at a thrift store. In 2020, Trevor Hayes ended up with the cards after his brother made a blind trade involving Pokémon cards. Neither knew what they had at first.Once collectors identified the 2017 cards, Hayes realised the unusual haul could bring in real money. He eventually made around $7,000 from most of the cards and used part of it to help his family during one of its hardest periods. How did a box nobody understood end up containing 100 Patrick Mahomes rookie cards?Thrift stores were already part of Hayes' routine long before the Mahomes cards appeared. He told FOX 4 that he visited them about four times a week, searching through items that could easily be dismissed as somebody else's unwanted belongings. Pokémon cards, Magic: The Gathering cards, electronics, paintings and antique toys were among the things he and his brother looked for.The brothers were familiar with collecting, but the Mahomes cards presented a different problem. There were 100 of them, all connected to the quarterback's 2017 rookie season, yet their exact identity and value were not immediately obvious.Mahomes had been selected No. 10 overall by the Chiefs in the 2017 NFL Draft, but his name alone was not enough for the brothers to understand what sat inside the box. The cards were from a less familiar Panini release, later identified as 2017 Panini Rated Rookie Personal Edition cards.Instead of discovering their value straight away, the box changed hands again.Hayes and his brother made a blind trade for a box of Pokémon cards. At the time, they did not have enough information to know they were giving up something collectors would eventually chase.Once Hayes had the cards, he knew he needed somebody familiar with sports cards to take a closer look.“I thought it was awesome,” Hayes told FOX 4. “I have to get these checked out and have somebody look at them.”That search eventually brought the cards to collectors. Hayes listed one card on Facebook Marketplace, and collectors recognised the unusual release. Sports Collectors Daily reported that a Kansas City card dealer bought 50 cards for $4,000, while collector Justinn Patton purchased another 20 for $2,500. Hayes also sold individual cards for around $200.FOX 4 reported that Hayes received around $7,000 for most of the unsigned cards and kept several for himself. Why did collectors find the story behind the 100 Patrick Mahomes cards so unusual?The cards were connected to Mahomes' first NFL season, but they were not simply a regular retail product that somebody had purchased and stored away.Sports Collectors Daily reported that the cards were linked to the 2017 NFLPA Rookie Premiere, an event involving 37 rookies that year. Panini produced personal-edition cards connected to the event, with some intended for players to sign.Collector Justinn Patton researched the release and contacted Panini while trying to understand the cards' history. According to Patton, Panini told him that 100 unsigned cards for each player were supposed to be destroyed after the event.That made the survival of the Mahomes batch particularly curious. Somehow, the cards avoided destruction and eventually reached a Goodwill store before making their way through the Hayes brothers' Pokémon-card trade.There was no public explanation for exactly how the cards left the event or who eventually donated them to Goodwill. Sports Collectors Daily reported that Panini did not provide an explanation for what happened to them.The box also contained an NFLPA watch and several bobbleheads, adding more memorabilia to a collection that initially looked like an ordinary thrift-store find.Hayes had another personal connection to Mahomes memorabilia. Before finding the 100 cards, his mother had bought him what appeared to be a signed Mahomes card. The family later discovered that the autograph was fake.For Hayes, that disappointment had been significant because the card meant something to him.“My heart hurt for him because I know how much that meant to him,” his mother, Marla Mosby, told FOX 4.The new collection gave Hayes another chance to own something connected to Mahomes' early NFL career. He eventually kept a few cards, with one hope still attached to them: getting Mahomes himself to sign one.“Keep it going. I’m loving everything that I see you’re doing on the field,” Hayes said in a message directed toward the Chiefs quarterback. “Maybe one day I can get one of these signed by you and cherish it forever.”How did the unexpected Patrick Mahomes money help Trevor Hayes' family?The cards became valuable to collectors, but their most important destination was not another sports-card collection.The money arrived during a difficult chapter for Hayes' family. Mosby had worked as a nurse before contracting West Nile Virus, after which she had to leave her job. She was also living with fibromyalgia.The family's financial situation had become severe enough that they had lost their home and cars.“It’s just been really rough on everybody,” Mosby said. “We lost our cars. We lost our house. We lost everything.”Hayes suddenly had thousands of dollars that could help his family. He put a down payment on a car for his mother and bought a used car for himself.“I was so grateful for the opportunity to make some money to help out the family and help myself out because it’s been a rough couple of months,” Hayes said.Mosby had spent much of her life being the person other people depended on, which made accepting help from her children an emotional experience.“I’ve always been the one to help everyone else my whole life. I’ve always been the one to give, and to be in a place to accept things from my kids is difficult,” she said. “It makes me proud. I feel humbled. I’m grateful.”Hayes also explained what he wanted to do with the opportunity the cards had given him.“It feels awesome,” he said. “That’s my whole thing. If I can help out my close friends and family, that’s all I really need in life.”There is an unusual irony in the way the story came together. The cards had been difficult for the brothers to identify, were traded away in exchange for Pokémon cards and had already passed through a Goodwill store without anyone apparently recognising their connection to Mahomes' rookie year.Their exact journey before Hayes found them remains unclear. Their value became much easier to understand once collectors recognised the release.A thrift-store box had travelled through Goodwill, a blind Pokémon-card trade and an uncertain period in which nobody knew exactly what it contained. Once collectors recognised the cards, the forgotten haul became around $7,000 in sales and gave Hayes a way to help his family.Among the few cards he kept, one unfinished part of the story remained: the hope that Patrick Mahomes might one day put his signature on one of them.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jerry Jones Admits Giants 'Were Better Than We Thought They Were' After Cowboys' Upset Loss
articles.summary: The New York Giants entered the 2026 campaign coming off three straight losing seasons, including a 4-13 effort in 2025, and the Dallas Cowboys may not have been fully prepared for the improved team they faced in Week 1.
articles.body:
The New York Giants entered the 2026 campaign coming off three straight losing seasons, including a 4-13 effort in 2025, and the Dallas Cowboys may not have been fully prepared for the improved team they faced in Week 1.

"They just did a good job all over," Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said during an appearance on 105.3 The Fan (h/t Bobby Kownack of NFL.com). "I will tell you, they were better than we thought they were. I'm anxious to see how New York continues to play. But really a combination of things. We didn't play as well as we should play and can play, but they played better than I thought they could."

New York won the Sunday night showdown 28-20 behind an excellent performance from quarterback Jaxson Dart.

He went 23-of-29 passing for 230 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions while adding 54 yards on the ground as a runner. Two of the touchdown passes went to new tight end Isaiah Likely, while running back Cam Skattebo also found the end zone on the ground.

It was an excellent start to the John Harbaugh tenure for the Giants and a sign they will be much more formidable under their new head coach. Considering Harbaugh was a Super Bowl champion who went to the playoffs 12 times with the Baltimore Ravens, perhaps that immediate improvement shouldn't have been so surprising.

But Jones' comments suggest the Cowboys were surprised by how effective the Giants were, as Dallas may have overlooked their season-opening opponent.

The Philadelphia Eagles are coming off five straight playoff appearances, so perhaps Jones and Co. assumed they would be the top challenger in the NFC East.

But the team owner also turned the attention to themselves.

"We didn't play well last week," he said. "What I meant to say was New York had really more to do with it than I thought they would. So, that's a factor. But Washington could have a lot to do with it here Sunday, too, so we've got to be ready to step up the level of play. There's no question."

It will be up to the Cowboys to play better in Sunday's contest against the Washington Commanders, otherwise they will be staring at an 0-2 start and a daunting hole to climb out of in the early playoff race.

articles.title: Puka Nacua injury update: Rams star wideout expected to be a game-time decision due to hip and groin injuries
articles.summary: Puka Nacua did not practice Friday or Saturday due to hip and groin issues.
articles.body:
Coming off a surprising loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1, the Los Angeles Rams need to bounce back against the New York Giants in Week 2 to live up to their status as Super Bowl contenders. But that task could prove difficult, as star wideout Puka Nacua will reportedly be a game-time decision for Monday's game due to hip and groin injuries, per ESPN.

After a modest performance in the team's 27-7 loss to the 49ers, in which he caught five passes for 74 yards, Nacua was able to get on the practice field Thursday. But the wideout unexpectedly did not practice Friday, with head coach Sean McVay saying Nacua "didn't feel totally like himself" during Thursday's practice. The Rams eventually listed Nacua on the team's injury report with a hip issue.

After Nacua failed to practice Saturday, McVay added another ailment to the list, saying Nacua was dealing with "a little bit of soreness" to his groin, per ESPN. Despite not practicing both days, Nacua was listed as questionable on the team's final injury report.

While a questionable designation often results in a player trying to gut it out, McVay said Saturday that Nacua would be a true game-time decision in Week 2, per ESPN.

"Whether or not he plays is to be determined," McVay said. "And so we'll see how he's feeling."

It's a concerning development for Nacua, who — on top of playing Monday night — already had additional days to recover following the team's Week 1 game against the 49ers. That game aired Thursday night in the United States, giving Nacua a full 10 days to rest up for Week 2.

When healthy, Nacua is considered one of the best receivers in football. After gaining 1,715 receiving yards and scoring 10 touchdowns last season, Nacua was named a first-team All-Pro for the first time in his career.

The 25-year-old has battled minor injuries and ailments since being drafted in 2023. A knee issue caused Nacua to miss five games in 2024 and an ankle issue forced him to miss a game last season. He's popped up on the injury report other times, but has usually played through issues.

Who would replace Puka Nacua for Rams in Week 2?

If Nacua is unable to go in Week 1, veteran Davante Adams would serve as the team's de-facto No. 1 option against the Giants. Jordan Whittingham and Tutu Atwell could also see increased snaps if Nacua is out. The team could also feature tight end Terrance Ferguson more as a pass catcher if Nacua is unable to do his usual middle-of-the-field work.

Regardless of Nacua's status, the Rams need to turn in a much better performance in Week 2. After a listless outing in Week 1, the Rams can't afford to open the year 0-2, not when the team entered the year as one of the Super Bowl favorites.

articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers sent scouts around the country this weekend to check out prospects for the 2027 NFL Draft. This includes having representatives at two games that featured a pair of the top quarterback prospects.

Pittsburgh sent representatives to the USC versus Rutgers and USC quarterback Joyden Maiava. Maiava ia a big, athletic thrower with a strong arm and great leadership who needs to show more consistency. USC got the win over Rutgers in a shootout, 42-35. Maiava threw went 20-for-32 and finished with 272 passing yards and two passing touchdowns and no interceptions.

The Steelers also sent scouts to Notre Dame versus Michigan State, featuring Fighting Irish quarterback CJ Carr. Carr was relatively quiet in the 27-10 win with just 234 passing yards on 18-of-24 throwing. Carr didn't throw a touchdown but did have a nine-yard rushing score.

Most pundits consider Carr a fringe first-round option who could solidify his spot at the third or fourth quarterback off the board with a strong season. Maiava is more of a wildcard in the draft but would be a nice value pick in the late second or third round.

articles.title: Patriots' Christian Gonzalez ‘Excited’ for Matchup Against Steelers Star in Week 2 NFL Game
articles.summary: Christian Gonzalez aims to step it up against one of the NFL’s top receivers.
articles.body:
After signing a massive extension, Christian Gonzalez looks to prove his value for the Patriots . That includes facing a top-tier receiver when the team takes on the Steelers in Week 2.

When the Patriots face the Steelers at Gillette Stadium , Gonzalez will have the opportunity to take on DK Metcalf , someone he hasn't played against since his second season in the NFL.

Gonzalez had 59 tackles in 2024, with two interceptions in 16 games. When the Patriots faced the Seahawks on September 14, Metcalf, with Seattle then, caught 10 passes for 129 yards, scoring a touchdown in a 23-20 Seattle win . Gonzalez had six tackles that game.

Metcalf signed with the Steelers last year. He had over 850 receiving yards, the lowest yard total in his career. At 6-foot-4, he is an intimidating figure. Gonzalez doesn't seem to mind. He's ready to compete against him again.

"Obviously a very strong, physical receiver. Very fast. Can run. They do a lot with him. I mean, [I'm] just excited for the matchup. I respect his game. He's been doing it for a while. He's been a No. 1 receiver in this league," Gonzalez said via Heavy . "I saw him in my second year last year… I'm just excited for another opportunity."

A 2023 NFL Draft pick, Gonzalez, in his fourth NFL season, agreed to a four-year, $135 million extension, making him the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history. He had two pass breakups and two tackles against the Seahawks during Week 1.

With another opportunity to play against Metcalf, Gonzalez aims to step it up against one of the NFL's top receivers.
